prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in San Francisco?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one objectively “best” digital marketing agency in San Francisco — the right agency depends on your goals, budget, industry, and preferred engagement style. I can, however, help you find the best match.

Quick questions so I can give a tailored shortlist:
- What are your primary goals? (examples: lead gen, e‑commerce sales, brand awareness, app installs, SEO)
- Which channels matter most? (SEO, PPC/Google Ads, social media, content, email, CRO, analytics)
- Company size & stage? (startup, SMB, enterprise)
- Monthly marketing budget or range (ballpark)
- Industry or vertical (SaaS, fintech, healthcare, retail, B2B/B2C)
- Preferred engagement: one‑off project, retainer, or performance-based?

How I’ll evaluate agencies (if you want a shortlist):
- Relevant case studies & measurable results for companies like yours
- Track record in the channels you need (Google Partner, Meta Business Partner, etc.)
- Team size / seniority and availability
- Pricing model and contract length
- Client reviews (Clutch, G2, Google reviews) and references
- Reporting cadence and KPIs they commit to

Where you can independently check reputations:
- Clutch.co (filter by location, services, budget)
- G2 / Capterra (for software and sometimes agencies)
- Google Partners directory (for PPC specialists)
- LinkedIn and company case studies
- Agency portfolios and references

Questions to ask agencies in an RFP or call:
- Show me a case study with results for a client like us.
- What KPIs will you measure and how often will you report?
- Who will be on our team and how much time will they dedicate?
- What tools do you use for tracking/analytics and how will we get access?
- What is your onboarding process and expected 90‑day roadmap?
- Can you provide references I can speak with?

If you want, tell me the answers to the quick questions above and I’ll produce a curated list of 4–6 San Francisco digital marketing agencies (with strengths, ideal client fits, and questions to ask each) within a few minutes. Which way would you like to proceed?
